rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday Cantonese word for a worker’s salary or pay.

example.english: My salary isn't high, but at least the job is stable.
example.traditional: 我份人工唔算高，但勝在份工穩定。
example.jyutping: ngo5 fan2 jan4 gung1 m4 syun3 gou1 daan6 sing3 zoi6 fan6 gung1 wan2 ding6

rows.note: A speaker uses this as a more neutral or formal alternative when referring to salary as fixed employment income.

example.english: The company deposits my salary directly into my bank account on the fifth of every month.
example.traditional: 公司會喺每月五號將薪水直接過入戶口。
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 wui2 hai2 mui5 jyut6 ng5 hou6 zoeng1 san1 seoi2 zik6 zip3 gwo3 jap6 wu6 hau2

rows.note: A speaker uses this casual word when focusing on the pay received from a job, especially around payday.

example.english: It's payday; as soon as I get my salary, I have to pay the rent.
example.traditional: 出糧喇，我一收到糧就要交租。
example.jyutping: ceot1 loeng4 laa3 ngo5 jat1 sau1 dou2 loeng4 zau6 jiu3 gaau1 zou1
